section: Earthquakes - causes, seismic waves, measurement, distribution, effects
subsections: Volcanoes in India - active vs dormant, Deccan Traps origin

accepted.s:
With reference to seismic waves, consider the following statements:
1. S-waves are transverse waves.
2. S-waves can propagate through liquids.
3. The absence of S-waves beyond about 105° from the epicentre is evidence that the outer core is liquid.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: S-waves involve shear motion perpendicular to the direction of travel and propagate only through solids. Their absence beyond about 105° indicates the liquid nature of the outer core.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the statement that reverses the solid-only property of S-waves.
accepted.sec: Seismic waves - order, motion, damage  [other exams]

accepted.s: Love and Rayleigh waves are collectively classified as:
accepted.x: Love and Rayleigh waves move along the Earth's surface and are classified as surface waves.
accepted.tq: Test the exact classification of closely related seismic waves.
accepted.sec: Seismic waves - order, motion, damage  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the movement and damaging potential of surface waves?
o: They move through the outer core and cause limited damage.
They arrive last and generally cause the greatest damage.
They arrive first and produce compressional motion only.
They travel only through liquids and have no particle motion.
accepted.x: Surface waves arrive after the body waves and usually cause the greatest damage. Love waves show side-to-side motion, while Rayleigh waves have a rolling motion.
accepted.tq: Compare arrival time, motion and damage rather than memorising one feature alone.
accepted.sec: Seismic waves - order, motion, damage  [other exams]

accepted.s: At the Mohorovicic discontinuity, the speed of P-waves increases approximately from:
accepted.x: The speed of P-waves jumps from about 6.9 km/s to 8.1 km/s at the Moho, named after Mohorovicic.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct numerical range from the two values forming the discontinuity.
accepted.sec: Seismic waves - order, motion, damage  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The outer core of the Earth is considered liquid.
Reason (R): S-waves do not pass beyond approximately 105° from the earthquake epicentre.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. Since S-waves cannot travel through liquids, their absence beyond the shadow zone supports the conclusion that the outer core is liquid.
accepted.tq: Check whether the seismic observation directly explains the inference about the Earth's interior.
accepted.sec: Seismic waves - order, motion, damage  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following belts is associated with the greatest concentration of earthquakes in the world?
accepted.x: The Circum-Pacific belt, also called the Ring of Fire, contains the world's greatest concentration of earthquakes and is associated largely with subduction around the Pacific basin.
accepted.tq: Use the ranking of earthquake belts to select the most active belt.
accepted.sec: World distribution

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Belt)
a. Pacific Ring of Fire
b. Mid-Atlantic belt
c. Mediterranean-Himalayan belt
 d. Hotspot belt

List-II (Plate setting or process)
i. Mantle plume beneath a moving plate
 ii. Divergent ridge
 iii. Subduction around a basin
 iv. Continental collision

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Pacific Ring of Fire is linked to subduction, the Mid-Atlantic belt to a divergent ridge, the Mediterranean-Himalayan belt to continental collision, and hotspots to mantle plumes.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure plate-setting pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong association.
accepted.sec: World distribution

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Chile lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire, not the Mid-Atlantic belt. Iceland is associated with the Mid-Atlantic belt, the Himalayas with the Alpine-Himalayan belt, and Hawaii with a hotspot.
accepted.tq: Find the location that belongs to a different seismic belt.
accepted.sec: World distribution

accepted.s: The earthquakes associated with mid-oceanic ridges are generally:
accepted.x: Mid-oceanic ridge earthquakes are generally shallow and milder, reflecting activity at divergent plate boundaries.
accepted.tq: Use the depth-and-severity comparison among the major earthquake belts.
accepted.sec: World distribution

accepted.s:
Which of the following 2026 earthquake events was reported with the correct magnitude and location?
1. Flores, Indonesia — magnitude 7.7
2. Colombia — magnitude 7.4
3. Kyushu, Japan — magnitude 7.1
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The reported 2026 events included the magnitude 7.7 Flores earthquake, the magnitude 7.4 Colombia earthquake and the magnitude 7.1 Kyushu earthquake.
accepted.tq: Verify each location–magnitude pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: World distribution

accepted.s: The 2026 earthquake in Colombia mentioned in the seismic-event record occurred on:
accepted.x: The Colombia earthquake of magnitude 7.4 was reported on 12 August 2026 and caused more than 100 deaths.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced dates by matching the event with its location.
accepted.sec: World distribution

accepted.s: Which combination of conditions is most conducive to the generation of a tsunami?
o: Magnitude below 5.0, deep focus and horizontal movement only
Magnitude above 6.5, shallow focus and vertical uplift of the sea floor
Volcanic ash fall without any displacement of water
Deep continental earthquake and subsidence of an inland basin
accepted.x: A tsunami generally requires an earthquake of magnitude greater than 6.5, a focus shallower than approximately 70 km and vertical uplift of the sea floor.
accepted.tq: Apply the necessary-condition test instead of relying on magnitude alone.
accepted.sec: Effects - tsunami, landslides, liquefaction, fires

accepted.s: Approximately what proportion of tsunamis originate from megathrust earthquakes at subduction zones?
accepted.x: More than 80 percent of tsunamis originate from megathrust earthquakes occurring at subduction zones.
accepted.tq: Select the quantitative threshold associated with the dominant tsunami source.
accepted.sec: Effects - tsunami, landslides, liquefaction, fires

accepted.s:
Match the earthquake effect with the region or cause most closely associated with it:

List-I (Effect)
a. Landslides
b. Liquefaction
c. Seismic seiches
 d. Fires

List-II (Associated setting or cause)
i. Broken gas and power lines
 ii. Lakes and reservoirs
 iii. Fragile Himalaya and North-East
 iv. Soft soils of the Indo-Gangetic Plain

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Earthquakes trigger landslides in the fragile Himalaya and North-East, liquefaction in soft Indo-Gangetic soils, seiches in lakes and reservoirs, and fires through broken gas and power lines.
accepted.tq: Match each hazard with its distinctive physical setting or immediate cause.
accepted.sec: Effects - tsunami, landslides, liquefaction, fires

accepted.s: Narcondam, located in the Andaman Sea, is associated with which of the following?
o: An extinct volcanic hill and the Asiatic lion
A dormant volcano and the Narcondam hornbill
India's only active volcano and the Nicobar pigeon
A flood-basalt plateau and the Great Indian bustard
accepted.x: Narcondam is a dormant volcano in the Andaman Sea and is the home of the Narcondam hornbill.
accepted.tq: Combine location, volcanic status and associated species to resolve a confusable pair.
accepted.sec: Volcanoes in India - active vs dormant, Deccan Traps origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Deccan Traps?
o: Fissure-related flood-basalt outpourings on the Maharashtra Plateau near the end of the Cretaceous
An intrusive granite batholith formed in Ladakh during the Cenozoic Era
A chain of dormant volcanic cones formed in the Andaman Sea during the Quaternary period
A group of extinct volcanic hills confined to Kutch
accepted.x: The Deccan Traps are fissure or flood-basalt outpourings on the Maharashtra Plateau that occurred at the end of the Cretaceous and are linked to the Reunion hotspot.
accepted.tq: Use origin, location and geological age together rather than a single keyword.
accepted.sec: Volcanoes in India - active vs dormant, Deccan Traps origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Deccan Traps are linked in origin with the:
accepted.x: The Deccan Traps are linked to activity of the Reunion hotspot near the end of the Cretaceous.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among similarly named hotspot examples using the associated landform.
accepted.sec: Volcanoes in India - active vs dormant, Deccan Traps origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A mud volcano at Diglipur is distinguished from a lava volcano because it ejects:
accepted.x: The Diglipur mud volcano ejects mud, water and methane rather than lava. Its activity is driven by tectonic pressure on the active Andaman Arc subduction zone.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a process by its actual ejecta rather than by the word volcano.
accepted.sec: Volcanoes in India - active vs dormant, Deccan Traps origin  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lopolith — wavy mass in a folded structure
Phacolith — wavy mass at the base of a syncline or top of an anticline
Laccolith — vertical wall cutting across rock beds
accepted.x: A phacolith is a wavy intrusive mass occurring at the base of a syncline or the top of an anticline. A lopolith is saucer-shaped, a laccolith is dome-shaped with a flat base, and a dyke is a vertical wall.
accepted.tq: Match each intrusive form with its distinctive shape or structural position.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which intrusive volcanic body is a huge dome of granite cooled deep within the crust and commonly forms the core of mountains?
accepted.x: A batholith is a huge dome-like mass of granite that cools deep in the crust and may form the core of a mountain range.
accepted.tq: Identify the landform from its scale, composition and depth of emplacement.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about intrusive volcanic forms:
1. A laccolith is dome-shaped and has a flat base.
2. A lopolith is saucer-shaped.
3. A sill is a horizontal sheet parallel to the rock beds.
4. A dyke is a vertical wall cutting across the beds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. These forms are distinguished mainly by their shape and their relation to the surrounding rock beds.
accepted.tq: Check each form against its geometric description and relation to bedding.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Deccan Traps were fed by which type of intrusive structure cutting across the rock beds?
accepted.x: Dykes are vertical walls that cut across rock beds and fed the fissure eruptions associated with the Deccan Traps in western Maharashtra.
accepted.tq: Connect the structural form of an intrusion with its role in feeding surface lava.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Ladakh Magmatic Arc lies between which two suture zones?
o: Main Boundary and Main Central suture zones
accepted.x: The Ladakh Magmatic Arc is located in the Trans-Himalaya between the Indus and Shyok suture zones.
accepted.tq: Use the paired geographical boundaries to identify the magmatic arc.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the geological development of the Ladakh Magmatic Arc?
o: It formed when the Neo-Tethys plate subducted under Eurasia and underwent a batholith phase from about 160 Ma to less than 45 Ma.
It formed from the Reunion hotspot during the end of the Cretaceous and consists only of flood basalts.
It formed at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge through present-day divergent movement.
It developed when the Indian plate subducted beneath the Pacific plate during the Quaternary period.
accepted.x: The Ladakh Magmatic Arc formed through subduction of the Neo-Tethys plate beneath Eurasia and experienced a batholith phase from approximately 160 Ma to less than 45 Ma.
accepted.tq: Combine the tectonic process with the geological time interval and reject unrelated settings.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an extrusive volcanic landform?
accepted.x: Lava plateaus, cinder and composite cones, craters, calderas and lava flows are extrusive volcanic landforms. Batholiths, lopoliths and phacoliths are intrusive forms.
accepted.tq: Separate surface-formed extrusive features from underground intrusive bodies.
accepted.sec: Volcanic landforms - intrusive and extrusive  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
